## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Februar 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.97
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.97
- Datum: 02.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah and Manfred, I write to you as short and clear as possible
without to alter the facts; I suppose you want to know my sincere impression.
We took today Eva from Mr Salmons house who was so kind to bring us over
with the car to Croton. The Salmons house is charming and I must say frankly
it was not Salmons fault if all did not work as we hoped. He is a very nice
fellow, and has given Eva all possible care and love. His weakness is perhaps
that he wants a little too much ~~admires~~ {to be} admired, loved
and thanked. And it seems that Eva by a kind of unconscious opposition has
just this refuses to him, she treated him (I have observed it myself) in a bit
cold and ironic way just because he wanted effusion and tenderness. Mr
Salmon and I agreed upon several points, especially about the question of letters.
As myself he was disappointed (and suspected an indifference of the heart
or the imagination) that she has always ~~been~~ pushed and forced to write to
you and he called quite rightly her letters to you „masterpieces of lack of
information“ She is indeed clever and yet enough not only to write to you
her silly „It has been nice“ but to think over what she has to report over
her school, her daily life, to give details and to understand better in
what danger and plight you live. All this I said her most seriously also for
my part, as it was really unpardonable, that she thanked my sister in law, who
went in aid of the Christmas trouble to buy her presents, just four weeks after
and that she had not the thought herself to write a line to her grandmother
in six months. As to the piano-playing her ambition is much greater than
her eagerness to practice; she is, I believe, just in an age or a transition,
where one must beware her of certain „Wurschtigkeit“ of sentiment and care-
lessness. Therefore I am glad that she is now at Mrs Schaeffer, who by having
educated six of her own children {and will look after her in} a more continental way will be much
more efficient. The boarding house is beautifully situated but, what I do not
want to conceal from you, run on very modest conditions. Eva will not
find the commodities of Salmons, not be the centre of attention, but to have
to clean her boots, her room. But believe me, a real American boarding school
would have brought silliness {and} superficiality and as the future of us all
is very obscure, I am convinced that it is better if she gets accustomed to
modest surroundings. The school seems to be excellent and as to Alfred
Schaeffer I know him since years - he is upright and a completely immature
little men, for whom his very effective wife cares like for a child - she
pleases me very much and we have the best feeling, that Eva is in units of the other children will
have a good time. Mr Salmon will continue to look after her and we ourselves will as to far as possible
for not to come again to Croton. Thats all and please - more to both both as soon as possible
Please write to Salmons - they have really been very nice to her.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf einem Blatt, beidseitig beschrieben. Der Text am linken Rand und am rechten Rand ist vertikal geschrieben. Die Tinte ist violett.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Korrekturen und der vertikalen Randnotizen. Die Tinte ist klar erkennbar.
